policy: Unknown or unpublished native semantics do not block empirical search. Every sprayable row uses source expressions with defined semantics, installed-driver ISA inspection, and a runtime or consumer-level correctness oracle before promotion.

candidates.consumer: packed tensor windows, optical-flow rolling windows, byte repacking
candidates.search: 64-bit concatenation in both orders; 32-bit shift/or in both orders; fixed 1/2/3-byte rolling windows
candidates.oracle: amd_vulkan_candidate_verify

candidates.consumer: bitstream/address packing and fused shift windows
candidates.search: 64-bit concatenation and 32-bit shift/or in both operand orders with dynamic 1..31-bit windows
candidates.oracle: amd_vulkan_candidate_verify

candidates.consumer: packed byte/nibble routing, tensor packing, optical-flow windows
candidates.search: byte reversal, interleaves, fixed cross-source permutations, dynamic two-source byte selection
candidates.oracle: amd_vulkan_candidate_verify

candidates.consumer: packing, masks, quantization and address manipulation
candidates.search: masked two-source select and three-input Boolean forms; expand with truth-table variants after first hardware run
candidates.oracle: amd_vulkan_candidate_verify

candidates.consumer: optical flow, filters, packed luma and future byte kernels
candidates.search: independent lane average variants with alternating rounding bits
candidates.oracle: amd_vulkan_candidate_verify plus math semantic verifier

candidates.consumer: FSR4 INT8 and future INT4/INT16 quantized kernels
candidates.search: same-sign and mixed-sign canonical extraction/multiply/add graphs for 2x16, 4x8 and 8x4
candidates.oracle: compiler semantic tests; add runtime integer-dot oracle for any nonstandard hit before APUSR use

candidates.consumer: future quantized kernels with saturating accumulation
candidates.search: direct SPV_KHR *DotAccSat versus independently widened 64-bit accumulation plus explicit signed/unsigned clamp
candidates.oracle: qualification boundary vectors around INT32/UINT32 overflow and saturation points before canonical promotion

candidates.consumer: FSR4 FP16 model operators and mixed-precision bookends
candidates.search: native half inputs with separate FP32 and FP16 accumulation contracts
candidates.oracle: amd.dot.f16.hlsl plus future runtime FP16 numerical oracle

candidates.consumer: future BF16 model/matrix paths
candidates.search: genuine BFloat16KHR scalar/vector types; exact KHR/VALVE dot contracts; scalar/vector OpFConvert with bit-preserving uint transport only at the HLSL boundary
candidates.oracle: BF16 special-value/rounding corpus; BF16->F32 is exact, while F32->BF16 narrowing must not be promoted to bit-exact parity until the required rounding behavior is pinned
candidates.reason: First-class BF16 ingress now exists. Stochastic-rounding AMD cvt_sr forms and a Vulkan contract that pins a particular F32->BF16 narrowing result remain separately blocked.

candidates.consumer: FSR4 FP16 reduction trees
candidates.search: fixed XOR stages 1/2/4/8/16/32 matching imported APUSR reduction trees
candidates.oracle: amd.intrinsics.lane-xor.hlsl; consumer-level active-lane comparison before replacement

candidates.consumer: reductions, stencil exchange and future matrix staging
candidates.search: lane +/- fixed constants with explicit self-fill boundaries plus 16-lane row-local rotates with wrap
candidates.oracle: amd.crosslane.neighbor.hlsl structural semantics; wave32/wave64 boundary-lane runtime corpus during qualification

candidates.consumer: manual FSR4 reduction trees and auto exposure
candidates.search: direct WaveActive sum/min/max versus explicit XOR butterfly trees matching APUSR generated reductions
candidates.oracle: fully active integer equivalence in probe inputs; active-mask, NaN, signed/unsigned and wave32/wave64 differential corpus during qualification

candidates.consumer: FSR4 post_common, import/export, exposure and color transforms
candidates.search: direct tanh/pow versus exp/log identities over a constrained positive finite domain; native frexp/ldexp recovery retained in both variants
candidates.oracle: dense numerical sweep including NaN, Inf, subnormal, sign and consumer-derived ULP/error limits before promotion

candidates.consumer: FP16 bookends, tensor packing and resource IO
candidates.search: independent scalar FP32<->FP16 conversions versus paired PackF16x2/UnpackF16x2 spelling
candidates.oracle: all half boundary classes and tie-rounding cases during qualification

candidates.consumer: APUSR tiled INT8/FP16 kernels
candidates.search: four scalar groupshared words versus one uint4 groupshared transaction with identical barrier and per-lane data
candidates.oracle: runtime data-integrity test plus APUSR tile numerical comparison before consumer rewrite

candidates.consumer: matrix/tensor tile staging
candidates.search: none safely expressible through current shader frontend
candidates.oracle: tile copy and synchronization stress corpus
candidates.reason: LLVM AMDGPU has explicit async global/LDS intrinsics, but current DXC shader-facing SPIR-V/DXIL surfaces do not preserve equivalent async-transfer semantics. Ordinary load+groupshared-store is not an equivalent candidate.

candidates.consumer: matrix tile staging and packed tensor layouts
candidates.search: none with reliable transposed hardware identity through current DXC shader IR
candidates.oracle: tile-layout permutation and alignment corpus
candidates.reason: The AMDGPU backend has explicit transposed-load intrinsics; generic vector loads are not a reliable semantic transport for them.

candidates.consumer: weight/tensor streaming and large tiled passes
candidates.search: none through current HLSL shader surface
candidates.oracle: cache-neutral correctness plus counter/timing A/B
candidates.reason: Current DXC shader-facing SPIR-V/DXIL has no AMD GPU prefetch contract. CPU/generic LLVM prefetch does not count.

candidates.consumer: WMMA/VALU overlap, VMEM/LDS latency hiding, transcendental-heavy passes
candidates.search: requires real compiler/IR transport
candidates.oracle: identical output plus stable ISA scheduling and timing improvement
candidates.reason: These are AMDGPU scheduling directives, not arithmetic semantics. Current SPIR-V/DXIL shader contracts do not carry them.

candidates.consumer: future ultra-low-precision model and matrix paths
candidates.search: retain source and backend inventory now; execute only on hardware that can validate the native path
candidates.oracle: format-specific rounding/special-value/matrix numerical corpus
candidates.reason: No suitable validation hardware in the current APUSR qualification target.
